analogs.covers: Character on land: toys with its prey, naps in the bushes, stares down rivals, hisses at the nest, grooms and feeds its partner
Life in the water: dives and fishes with its lifelong partner, knows it by voice, huddles and breeds in a crowded beach colony

headline: A house cat on land and a penguin in the water: toys with what it catches, naps in the bushes and stares down rivals, then dives with its lifelong partner and breeds in a crowded beach colony.

setting.label: Rivers, coasts and seaways
setting.note: Semi-aquatic and nomadic. Migrates to dedicated courtship and nesting grounds where unlimited Austroraptor gather in a 'siege'; territorial over fallen logs and prime fishing spots.

playsLike: You are a medium semi-aquatic hunter bonded to one mate for life. On land you are a house cat: curious and a little aloof, napping in the bushes, staring rivals down and playing with anything small enough to carry. In the water you are a penguin: you dive and fish with your partner and travel to a crowded beach colony to court and nest. You eat the easy food first: fish, crabs, critters and scavenged meat. After that come offspring and small prey you can carry off, drown or smash on rocks. A pair hunts up to Medium tier, four together can mob a solo Large, and you flee every Apex carnivore.

why.text: Austroraptor "enjoy taking advantage of their ability to firmly hold small prey, often toying with them before killing them." A Deinonychus that swims free is nipped and taunted, then caught again, like a cat with a mouse.

Sleeps "in short periods sporadically through the day and night", tucked away in shrubs. Dominance is an intense stare, submission is looking away, and a parent hisses at any Austroraptor within a body length of the nest. That is house-cat body language.

why.trait: Curious, with a human on call
why.text: "Examine new things and new species very closely" and quietly follows new species. At a dead tree it calls until a larger creature pushes the log over, like a cat meowing until someone opens the door.
Pairs preen each other and present fish and critters to each other, and parents carry their chicks to safety in their mouths, as a mother cat carries her kittens.
"Every individual Austroraptor has a unique voice"; bonded pairs recognise each other at a great distance. Emperor penguins find their partner in the colony the same way (official inspiration).
Nests in the open on beaches close to other pairs, huddles against rain, snow and night, and its chicks cannot swim until they moult their down into "adult swimming feathers". All of that is penguin.
Medium tier, 2,100 combat weight, fast on land (sprint 1,100) and able to hold a water sprint for 250 s. At home on both.

notLike: House cats avoid water; Austroraptor dives for fun. That half is the penguin.
Cats hunt alone; Austroraptor hunts as a pair and joins four-strong mobs.
Penguins can't run; Austroraptor is quick on land.
twist: The fishing pose comes from the heron, the profile's other official inspiration: standing motionless in the shallows with wings spread as shade, or waiting on a fallen log above the water. Even the word for its gatherings, a 'siege', is borrowed from herons.
